title: Eyes Aching to See Him
note: Her eyes suffer in their haste to see him. This comes after she has wasted away in grief.

couplets.plain: Why do my eyes weep now? It was through their showing that I came to see this endless sickness.
couplets.pm: I came to know this unending sickness because my eyes showed me my lover. Why do those same eyes now weep, telling me to show him to them? Today too, only they can show him. How could I?
couplets.context: Her friend says her weeping eyes are losing their beauty and she must bear up. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Why do my eyes weep now?
links.reason: She faces her eyes, who weep though they brought the sickness on by showing him to her.

couplets.plain: These kohl-lined eyes looked without knowing what would come. Why do they now suffer, not understanding?
couplets.pm: My kohl-lined eyes looked at my lover that day without weighing what would follow: that he would go and not come back. Why do they suffer now, instead of reasoning that this came through them and must be borne? If you don’t guard against a thing, bearing it is all that’s left. Not even doing that is utter folly.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: These kohl-lined eyes looked without knowing what would come
links.reason: Blames her eyes for one rash look and asks why they suffer now.

couplets.plain: My eyes rushed to look, and now they weep by themselves. There is something laughable in this.
couplets.pm: These eyes rushed to look at my lover that day of their own accord, and now they sit weeping of their own accord. This folly is something for me to laugh at. It brings laughter from those who guard against a thing before it comes.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: There is something laughable in this

couplets.plain: My kohl-lined eyes have left in me a sickness I can’t escape or survive, and now they can’t weep, their water gone.
couplets.pm: That day my kohl-lined eyes fixed in me an endless sickness that I can’t escape. Now their water has dried up and they can’t even weep. They fixed it there by showing me one who would leave and not return. They did me harm first, and harm has come to them.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: they can’t weep, their water gone
links.reason: Her eyes left the sickness fixed in her, then ran dry.

couplets.plain: My eyes, which gave me a sickness of desire too great for the sea, now suffer and can’t close.
couplets.pm: My eyes gave me a sickness of desire so great that the sea seems small. For that evil deed they suffer too and can’t sleep. Desire came through seeing, so she blames the eyes for it. Their suffering is their weeping.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: The eyes that caused her sickness are themselves now suffering and sleepless.

couplets.plain: Oh, how sweet! The eyes that gave me this sickness have fallen into it themselves.
couplets.pm: The eyes that gave me this sickness of desire have themselves fallen into this sleepless weeping. How very sweet! To me, whom they made suffer, it is as if the pain had ended.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: Let them suffer and suffer till their water runs out, these eyes that longed and longed and begged to see him.
couplets.pm: Those eyes longed and melted that day and wouldn’t let him out of their sight. Let them suffer this sleepless weeping on and on, until the water inside them is gone!
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she
couplets.sensitive: wishes her own eyes wasted away as a punishment

links.quote: Let them suffer and suffer till their water runs out
links.reason: She curses her eyes for their longing gaze and wishes them dry.

couplets.plain: There is one who wanted me without cherishing me. Still, my eyes will not rest until they see him.
couplets.pm: The one who wanted me in words but not in his heart is right here. What use is that? My eyes won’t rest without seeing him. His actions showed no care, though he spoke of fearing to part and of coming back. I can bear it, but my eyes can’t. With another reading: are there any in the world who want one who doesn’t want them?
couplets.context: Her friend says he hasn’t really gone, he is here, and she must bear up until she sees him. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: There is one who wanted me without cherishing me
links.reason: States the fact of it: he wanted her without cherishing her, and still her eyes want him.

links.quote: my eyes will not rest until they see him

couplets.plain: When he doesn’t come they don’t sleep. When he comes they don’t sleep. Either way my eyes are in deep pain.
couplets.pm: When my lover hasn’t come, my eyes stay awake watching for him. When he has come, they stay awake fearing he will leave. Both ways they suffer past bearing. They will never have sleep.
couplets.context: Her friend says she must bear up and let her eyes sleep. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: When he doesn’t come they don’t sleep

couplets.plain: It isn’t hard for the town to find out the secret of those like me, whose eyes are beaten drums.
couplets.pm: The town finds it easy to learn the secret held in the hearts of those like me, whose eyes are drums being beaten. Eyes and drums alike tell the world outside what is inside. Though I hide it, these eyes make it known.
couplets.context: Her friend says she must hide his cruelty, so that the town won’t speak ill of him. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: It isn’t hard for the town to find out the secret
links.reason: The townsfolk read her secret straight off her eyes.
